intro: Choose the particle picture that matches the chemistry: how water molecules point at a cation or an anion, what is left after a reaction with a limiting reactant, which mixture is at equilibrium, and a strong acid against a weak one. Every wrong picture is a mistake readers see on real free-response answers, and the feedback says which one.
howItWorks:
• Ions in water (Unit 3): water's oxygen end is partially negative and its hydrogen ends partially positive. Oxygen points toward a cation; hydrogens point toward an anion (ion-dipole attraction).
  • Limiting reactant (Unit 4): count atoms before and after. The limiting reactant is gone, the excess is left over, and products form in the ratio of the coefficients.
  • Equilibrium (Unit 7): an equilibrium mixture keeps some of every species, and its counts give Q = K.
  • Acid strength (Unit 8): a strong acid ionizes completely; a weak acid is mostly un-ionized (a few percent, worked out exactly from Ka).

Each atom carries its symbol, so color is never the only cue, and each picture has a text description for screen readers. Pictures unlock with their units.
